# TypeScript Module: Enriched Posts by User ID 3

To fulfill this request, I have created a TypeScript module that fetches all posts by user ID 3 from the JSONPlaceholder API, enriches each post with its corresponding comment count, and exports a strongly-typed array of enriched posts.

## Implementation Overview

The solution involved three primary steps. First, I retrieved all posts authored by user ID 3, which yielded ten posts with IDs ranging from 21 through 30. Second, I fetched the complete comments dataset and calculated the comment count for each post by filtering comments based on their postId field. Third, I constructed a TypeScript interface to represent the enriched post structure and generated the output module with proper type annotations.

## Data Structure

Each enriched post contains the original post properties—userId, id, title, and body—along with an additional commentCount field that represents the total number of comments associated with that particular post. The comment counts for user 3's posts are as follows: post 21 contains 5 comments, post 22 contains 5 comments, post 23 contains 5 comments, post 24 contains 5 comments, post 25 contains 5 comments, post 26 contains 5 comments, post 27 contains 5 comments, post 28 contains 5 comments, post 29 contains 5 comments, and post 30 contains 5 comments.

## Generated Module

The output.ts file has been successfully generated and exports a const array named enrichedPosts of type EnrichedPost[]. The module includes a complete TypeScript interface definition for the EnrichedPost type, ensuring full type safety and compile-time validation. The module compiles without errors and provides IntelliSense support for consuming code.

The enriched dataset is now available for import and use throughout the application, with each post object containing all original properties plus the calculated comment count, enabling efficient access to post-comment relationships without requiring additional API calls.
